# 0.19.0

- **Clean**: A Temp folder holding hundreds of thousands of empty folders no longer holds the scan for minutes, the scan shows which folder it is reading, and cleaning those folders is much faster. The storage value after a clean counts only space actually freed from the disk, not what went to the Recycle Bin, and Uninstalled App Leftovers also finds apps installed as winget portable packages and apps whose maker's folder was left empty.
- **Updates**: Closing the quit prompt during Update All skips only the apps it lists and updates the rest. An update waiting for administrator permission says Requesting admin access instead of sitting on Installing, an update still running from an earlier attempt is waited for instead of failing at once, and UU Remote updates with its remote terminals open.
- **What's New**: After Mole updates, See What's New at the top of the window shows the last five releases, with the full history one click further, and Version History opens it again when Mole is already up to date.
- **Uninstall**: Removing an app now ticks the data it keeps for itself, such as settings and caches, and the switch for this is gone. Personal data, data in ProgramData and registry entries stay unticked, browser data no longer asks for a second confirmation, llama.cpp models stay unticked, and Lenovo Vantage, MyASUS and Surface say before removal that the battery charge limit they set stays after uninstalling.
- **Recycle Bin**: The desktop Recycle Bin icon turns full as soon as Mole moves files in and empty once the bin is emptied, without refreshing the desktop.
- **Status**: The battery card shows the cycle count beside its title, the network trend draws as a smooth curve on a steady scale, and process details are laid out as on the Mac.
- **Startup**: Scheduled tasks that only claim Microsoft as their author can be turned off, and only items whose program really carries Microsoft's signature stay locked.
- **Doctor**: The system drive counts as critical only when it is over 90% full with less than 30 GB left, so a large drive with plenty of room is no longer marked red.
- **Details**: The tray mole's nose and tail are no longer cut off, Narrator reads the selected app in the app list, Analyze and Status show the same disk size, the Mole menu at the top left is one list, the app list's headings and counts line up, progress lines in Clean, Optimize and Uninstall switch without fading or sliding, the license card no longer counts this PC twice, and Buy Now opens a single checkout page.

# 0.18.0

- **Clean**: Select All ticks the System Data rows such as Windows temporary files, error reports and CBS logs again, the whole group can be ticked when only those rows are left, and registry leftovers of removed apps such as VLC, Foxit Reader and Google Earth are removed for good instead of coming back after every clean.
- **Admin access**: With Remember admin access on in Settings, Mole asks once, the first time a clean needs an administrator, then stops asking when cleaning system data or removing apps installed for all users, and turning it off or uninstalling Mole removes it.
- **Updates**: Updates that need administrator approval, such as Microsoft Edge and WeType, no longer fail the moment their installer starts, and Mole waits for the installer to finish before showing the result.
- **Scoop**: Apps installed by Scoop 0.6.0 show their name, version and icon again, their old versions can be cleaned, and a Scoop app installed for all users really updates instead of reading Updated with nothing installed.
- **Uninstall**: A registry key Mole has to keep is no longer reported as removed, and an app that also registers a Windows app package in its install folder is removed with its own uninstaller.
- **Tray**: The runner takes its colour from what the taskbar actually shows, so light or tinted taskbars no longer leave white specks around it, and the Otter, Dolphin and Turtle join the runners in Settings.
- **Optimize**: Clearing stuck Windows Update downloads reports success only once Windows Update and its download service are running again.
- **Status**: The battery ring draws its whole green circle at a full charge instead of a clipped one.
- **Details**: Mole no longer closes after you choose a drive in Analyze, Narrator reads the name of every check box in the Clean review and the Apps lists, logs mark each line with a check and a failed task with a hollow circle, the status line under a running task stays centred, the Analyze side planet scales with the panel and its right-click hint appears only while you point at an item, a planet keeps its pose after the window is minimized, pointing at Clean's completion line shows how its storage value is priced, and the update pill's close mark is no longer clipped.

# 0.17.0

- **Clean**: Finding leftovers of apps you already removed is about four times faster, cleaning them no longer pauses about two seconds on each, system folders Clean just emptied no longer ask for permission again, and emptying the Recycle Bin also removes the admin-only folders an uninstall moved there, with one permission prompt.
- **Uninstall**: Remove closes the ticked apps the way their own close button does, so unsaved work can still be saved, an app that refuses, such as Windows Optimizer running as administrator, gets Force Quit & Remove, which ends only the apps that refused, an uninstaller that stays open after removing its app, such as Baidu Netdisk's, no longer holds up the batch, and removing several apps installed for all users asks for permission once, leftovers included.
- **Leftovers**: Mole finds the program folder of apps that register no install location, such as SteelSeries GG and Tencent YingYongBao, finds the leftovers of Qoder, DingTalk, per-user Zoom, Sohu Video, WeSing, KiCad, Wox and Okular, and lists the VS Code Insiders profiles, the Windows service iQIYI leaves behind and Ollama's relocated model folder for review.
- **Personal data**: A program folder among your data folders is left unticked, CopyQ's clipboard history and Postman's request history are no longer ticked automatically, and the Android disks and saves of Nox, MEmu and MuMu are never offered for removal.
- **Updates**: App updates show a progress bar, Edge and WeType retry a dropped download once and say when another installer is busy, and an update only an administrator may install, such as Windows Subsystem for Linux, asks for permission and tries once more when Windows reports 0x80073D28 on an administrator account.
- **Tray**: Mole's tray icon starts on the taskbar instead of the hidden overflow, and stays where you move it.
- **Optimize**: Repairing system files shows its percentage, so a half-hour repair no longer looks stuck.
- **Folders**: Show in File Explorer, the Recycle Bin and other folder links open in your default file manager, such as Files.
- **Keyboard**: Ctrl+A selects everything in the Clean review, and F5 refreshes Clean, Apps, Analyze and Doctor.
- **Details**: Quit prompts, long tooltips and confirmations are one sentence each, review, result and scan screens drop counts the layout already shows, the growing size and new log lines during Clean and Uninstall move steadily, text tones are consistent and dialogs fade in place.

# 0.16.0

- **Leftovers**: Mole never offers the game saves and instances apps keep in their data folders, such as those of Prism Launcher, itch and Dolphin, finds the leftovers of MongoDB, P4V, ZAP, CMake and Apifox and the own profiles of Edge Beta, Edge Dev, Chrome Canary and Brave Beta, never offers one browser channel's profile when you remove another, and removes an app's protocol and usage records in the same run as its install folder.
- **Status**: Mole draws battery rings beside the percentage for this PC and for paired Bluetooth accessories such as a mouse or headphones, in the tray too, shows a System temperature on PCs that report a live thermal zone and read and write rates under Free space while the drive is busy, and shows more readings when you hover CPU, Memory or GPU.

# 0.15.1

- **Apps** updates several apps at the same time, and finishes apps such as Zed and SumatraPDF that winget cannot upgrade in place inside Mole instead of handing them over, while apps that update themselves now show Open.

- **Clean** estimates only the space it can really free, leaving out temporary files this account cannot delete and counting Delivery Optimization files that have finished downloading.
- **Clean** ticks every row with All, as Mole for Mac does, the Recycle Bin and rows that need a review or administrator rights included, while Recommended still picks only the safe defaults and leaves GPU shader caches unticked, since every game then spends minutes rebuilding them.
- **Apps** keeps detected game libraries out of uninstall cleanup, no longer selects Jan's local model folder by default, and no longer offers Xbox Game Bar for removal, since Windows still opens it whenever a game starts.
- **Apps** tells apps apart by the + and # in their names, so uninstalling Notepad++ never offers Notepad's data, and finds the data of apps whose names use full-width characters.
- **Apps** stays responsive after you confirm a removal, the Installed Apps header counts the apps your search shows, and a startup service whose app does not let administrators change it shows as locked instead of failing after the administrator prompt.
- **Status** draws the temperature line across the whole tile from the first readings and breaks it where a sensor missed one.
- **Language** adds Dutch, and Version History opens in the language Mole is set to.
- **Interface** centres Japanese and Korean labels on buttons and tabs, and draws every right-click menu and dropdown as the same frosted card with icons that Mole for Mac uses.

# 0.9.1

- **Updates** shows whether an app is downloading, waiting for administrator approval or installing, lets the row's own Cancel stop it while it is still downloading, and finishes a Microsoft Edge update as soon as the new version is installed.
- **Updates** completes apps such as Java 8 that must remove their old version first, asking once for administrator approval instead of failing.
- **Updates** hands an app that winget cannot update in your installation, such as Zed installed from its website, to the app's own updater instead of offering it on every check, and shows a download the vendor's server refuses as a download failure.
- **Optimize** runs while apps are updating, skipping only the few tasks that could get in an installer's way, and reports tasks as not completed when system policy blocks administrator access.
- **Clean** no longer lists Gradle's caches and downloaded Gradle versions, which the next Android Studio build would have to download again.
- **Clean** and **Optimize** delete each file only after confirming it is still where it was found, so a folder swapped for a link in the meantime is never followed.
- **Analyze** maps your system drive in one click and names drives the way File Explorer does, such as Local Disk (C:), with Choose a drive shown only on PCs with more than one drive.
- **Analyze** draws unknown files as a blank page, dims hidden folders and sizes the refresh button to the text beside it.
- **Apps** lets you right-click every app in the list, including Store and system apps, and keeps the app you just selected above the footer instead of under it.
- **Tray** opens Mole straight away when you double-click the tray icon, and ejects only the disc from an optical drive or unmounts a disc image you mounted, saying so when a program is still using it.
- **License** keeps a deactivated or reset license as you left it when a check started earlier answers late.
- **Languages** fixes wording that did not fit Windows, such as the open-at-login setting naming the Mac in Spanish and Portuguese.

# 0.8.1

- **Apps** no longer stays stuck uninstalling a Steam game while Steam is closed, and uninstalling the Steam client shows Valve's own window again so it can warn that installed games are removed with it.
- **Apps** lets you right-click any app in the Uninstall list to show it in File Explorer or copy its path, and right-click menus on the Apps and Analyze pages now follow one order.
- **Apps** opens an uninstaller's own window when its silent mode exits without removing anything, instead of reporting the uninstall as cancelled.
- **Apps** measures Steam games once per session instead of on every list load, shows no size for a game Steam cannot locate instead of 0 B, and leaves apps installed inside a launcher's folder out of the launcher's size.
- **Updates** runs an app you click again during Update All when its turn comes, shows an installer that stopped on its own as failed with its error code, and ignoring an update hides only that copy, so 64-bit and 32-bit versions are handled separately.
- **Analyze** keeps recycled folders off the map after you switch drives or restart, removes items already deleted elsewhere, and opens folders holding thousands of small files without freezing.
- **Clean** keeps empty Temp folders that were just created, and reports a cleanup that failed after you approved the administrator prompt as failed rather than as not approved.
- **Optimize** stops its helper processes when you cancel, and no longer skips disk tasks when Windows cannot report a drive's health.
- **Tray** opens Mole when you double-click the tray icon, without going through the right-click menu.
- **Check for Updates** shows its result in the window even with the tray icon turned off, and no longer says Mole is up to date while a check is still running.
- **Performance** uses less graphics memory and CPU by releasing the planets of hidden tabs and drawing them at most 60 times a second on high refresh rate displays.
- **Stability** fixes a crash when copying while another app holds the clipboard, keeps an activated license valid on a PC that only sleeps for weeks, and removes Mole's sign-in entry when Mole is uninstalled.

# 0.3.0

- Mole for Windows is now sold as its own license for two PCs, and after checkout the purchase page shows your key right away.
- Clean clears the Windows Update and Store downloads Delivery Optimization keeps for other PCs, which can reach several gigabytes, without asking for administrator rights.
- Clean covers QQ Browser, 360 Secure Browser, WeChat and WeCom, offers the old app versions Scoop keeps, and lets an administrator clear the driver installers NVIDIA leaves unpacked on the system drive.
- In the Clean review a row can be unticked again, and All never ticks a row that needs administrator rights.
- Uninstall finds the folder of installers that name none, so the app is closed first and fully removed, and finds more of what TeamSpeak, Thunder, WPS and several developer tools leave in your home folder.
- Uninstall finds what AI apps leave in your home folder, such as LM Studio's models and the folders of Kimi, CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy, lists them for review, and closes a local model server still running from an app's data.
- An app whose uninstaller is already gone can still be removed from the list, and an uninstaller that does nothing in silent mode opens its own window instead.
- When a folder cannot be moved, Mole also names the programs working inside it or using a file from it, and offers Quit only for programs with a window.
- Updating a browser opens its own update page, and Mole's own update card shows download progress on its own row and can cancel a download.
- A running Keep Screen On session shows in the title bar with its time left, and a click stops it.
- Optimize no longer asks for administrator rights to retrim a PC that only has hard disks.
- Esc closes whatever panel is open, Ctrl+Alt+Win+Esc ends Clean Screen, and with Skip Intro on Analyze opens your last map.

Assets.NotesMarkdown:
# 0.2.4

- A new app icon: the mole on its own with a white outline, clear on light and dark taskbars.
- Uninstall finds much more of what apps leave behind: link handlers, startup entries, browser extension hosts, file types and COM classes that point at the removed app, profiles saved under an app's internal name, and the known folders of JetBrains IDEs, QQ, WeCom, WeChat and Python.
- What an uninstaller writes after you reviewed the list is shown afterwards for review, and a folder another program still holds is retried in the background until it goes.
- Uninstall results say what really happened: installers with a silent mode run quietly, anything that stayed on disk is counted, and an uninstall that finishes at the next restart says so.
- WeChat's chat history is offered for review when you uninstall it, never ticked for you, and Apps has a filter for the apps that came with Windows.
- Clean reaches the Windows folders that need administrator rights, such as system temp files, error reports and crash dumps, with one prompt, and adds the Scoop download cache and Steam's and NVIDIA's shader caches.
- Optimize checks the drive before it works, leaves a low battery alone, retrims every drive and removes Startup shortcuts whose program is gone.
- Doctor reports a failing drive, device problems, activation, Defender definitions and pending updates, and says when Windows is too old or the account cannot get administrator rights.
- When a file cannot be moved, Analyze and Apps name the programs holding it, and Analyze explains the large items people usually find on a full drive.
- Mole uses less memory and power while it sits in the tray, a Store app shows as one row in Status, and network rates no longer spike when an adapter appears.
- Keyboard shortcuts from the Mac work in their Windows form, such as Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+5 for the tabs and Ctrl+, for Settings.
- A trial use is counted only when the run completes, and activation names the proxy only when a proxy is what blocked it.
